faq.q: What is the Strait of Hormuz?
faq.a: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow, strategically important waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. It is a critical choke point for global oil and gas shipments, with a significant portion of the world's seaborne oil passing through it daily.

faq.q: How does an Iran deal affect global oil prices?
faq.a: A deal with Iran could lead to the easing of international sanctions, allowing Iran to export more crude oil. This increased supply entering the global market would typically lead to lower crude oil prices, assuming demand remains constant or grows at a slower pace.

faq.q: Why is gold considered an inflation hedge?
faq.a: Gold is considered an inflation hedge because it tends to retain its value or even appreciate during periods when the purchasing power of fiat currencies declines due to inflation. It is a tangible asset not tied to any specific government or economy.

faq.q: Should I invest in gold right now?
faq.a: Investment decisions should always align with your personal financial goals, risk tolerance, and overall asset allocation. While gold can be a good diversifier, its short-term movements are unpredictable. Consult a financial planner to see if gold fits into your portfolio.

faq.q: How does crude oil impact inflation in India?
faq.a: India imports a large majority of its crude oil. Higher global crude oil prices increase the cost of fuel and transportation, which then affects the prices of almost all goods and services, leading to higher domestic inflation. Conversely, lower oil prices help temper inflation.

faq.q: What are the different ways to invest in gold?
faq.a: You can invest in gold through physical gold (jewellery, coins, bars), Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) issued by the RBI, or gold mutual funds. Each option has its own benefits regarding liquidity, purity, and taxation.
